fact_text: K-Electric's predecessor, the Karachi Electric Supply Corporation (KESC), began in 1913 as a government institution.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: In 1999 KESC's administrative control was handed to the Pakistan Army's engineering corps to curb electricity theft.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: By 2005 KESC was making heavy losses amid massive power theft, and the government was trying to sell it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: In 2003 the Privatisation Commission of Pakistan announced the sale of 73% of KESC's stake.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: At the KESC auction on 4 Feb 2005, a Saudi group, Kunooz Al Watan, won with a bid of 1.65 per share (currency not stated in the video).
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: The Kunooz Al Watan winner failed to deposit the payment, so its deal was cancelled; the runner-up consortium was asked to match the price, did so, and the sale closed in Nov 2005.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: After the 2005 sale the government kept 24% of KESC, while control passed to Saudi Al Jomaiah Group and Kuwait National Industries Group through KES Power, a Cayman Islands shell company.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: The reporter said the Saudi and Kuwaiti owners struggled to run the utility effectively despite paper profits in the years after the 2005 sale.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: In 2008 the Saudi and Kuwaiti owners approached Karachi-born private equity figure Arif Naqvi of the Abraaj Group.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Abraaj bought a 53.8% stake in KES Power, the Cayman holding company that controlled K-Electric.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Abraaj's investment in KES Power was reported at 370 to 390 million US dollars; the value shown is the lower figure of that range.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Abraaj's direct equity in KESC was only about 35%, yet its control of KES Power gave it management control of the whole utility.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Under Abraaj's management about 7,000 surplus staff were downsized.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Under Abraaj's management more than 1 billion US dollars went into power plants and network upgrades.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: According to an academic case study, KESC posted a profit in 2011 and 2012, its first in 17 years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: In 2013 KESC was rebranded as K-Electric.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: On 28 Oct 2016 Abraaj and Shanghai Electric, a Chinese state-owned company, signed a 1.77 billion US dollar deal for a 66.4% stake in K-Electric.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: The 2016 signing came in the peak era of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, and industry experts called it one of the largest corporate acquisitions in Pakistan's history.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: The reporter said the Shanghai Electric deal stalled on national security clearances, regulatory approvals and lengthy tariff disputes with NEPRA.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Some government sources claimed the Privatisation Commission asked for a review of the acquisition agreement; the reporter noted Abraaj refused to show it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: According to K-Electric's own statements, government departments owed it over Rs158 billion by April 2019, Rs32 billion of it from the Karachi Water Board alone.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Sui Southern Gas Company claimed that by 2020 K-Electric owed it roughly Rs16 billion including markups, a counter-claim in the receivables dispute.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Large unpaid receivables from government buyers drain a power distributor's cash and can stall the sale of the distributor, as the reporter argued in the K-Electric case.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: In an email quoted in a book review, Arif Naqvi wrote that the K-Electric sale to Shanghai Electric was the ultimate fix for Abraaj's liquidity crisis.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: According to the Financial Times, Abraaj Holdings would have pocketed roughly 450 million US dollars in cash had the ownership transfer completed by late 2017.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: The reporter said Abraaj took 16 years to build but collapsed in just four months.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: In mid-2018 Abraaj Group entered provisional liquidation in the Cayman Islands.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Allegations surfaced in 2018 that money from Abraaj's health fund, backed by investors such as the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, was misallocated; Naqvi consistently denied wrongdoing.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: In April 2019 London police arrested Arif Naqvi in connection with the Abraaj Group case.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: The reporter said K-Electric did not destroy Abraaj, but the endless delays in the K-Electric exit hastened Abraaj's collapse.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: In 2022 Shariar Chishti's Asia Park Investments, through a British Virgin Islands entity, bought Abraaj's legacy 53.8% stake in KES Power after the Cayman court approved the sale.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Al-Jomaiah and partner Denham argued that changing management required shareholder consent, and fired back against the sale.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Al-Jomaiah's Shan Ashari argued that K-Electric's ownership is tied to national security and demands multiple layers of clearance.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: In October 2022 the Sindh High Court issued a stay order freezing changes to K-Electric's board.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: By July 2023 the Cayman court ordered legal challenges in Pakistan to be dropped; the appeals that followed were dismissed by the Privy Council.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: By January 2026 the cases on K-Electric were due to be withdrawn.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: On 15 Apr 2026 Shariar Chishti was named chairman of K-Electric's board of directors.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: On 16 Jan 2026 Saudi and Kuwaiti investors, who hold roughly 31% of K-Electric, started a 2 billion US dollar international arbitration claim against Pakistan.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: The arbitration claim, as reported, cites the blocking of the Shanghai Electric deal, unpaid receivables and interference with tariffs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: On 9 Sep 2025 Shanghai Electric's board formally decided to cancel and exit the 1.77 billion US dollar K-Electric deal.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Shanghai Electric said the other party failed to fulfil the closing conditions, which was its reason for cancelling the deal.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Reuters reported that K-Electric's fractured ownership structure became a major red flag for Shanghai Electric.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: Investors argued the government delayed the deal, while Shanghai Electric argued the closing conditions were never met; both narratives are on record.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: The reporter said red tape and regulatory delays have long been a massive hurdle between Pakistan and foreign investment.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: The reporter said the K-Electric saga damaged Pakistan's privatisation image, making it harder to attract foreign investors.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)

fact_text: K-Electric supplies power to Karachi, a city of more than 20 million people.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Karachi To Cayman Islands: The Untold Story of K-Electric | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-30)
